name: MileQuill Distance Shipping Rates
author: wajahat10947

sections.description:
MileQuill Distance Shipping Rates registers a native WooCommerce shipping-zone method. Offer free shipping within a configured driving distance and a flat shipping charge beyond that distance up to a maximum limit. Choose a standard single shipping address or two independent complete addresses for moving, rental and pickup services. Each distance is measured from the configured origin.

  • Native shipping-zone method with configurable customer-facing title and tax status.
  • Single address mode uses the standard WooCommerce shipping destination (billing address when shipping to the billing address).
  • Dual address mode supports new or existing checkout full-address fields.
  • Editable US origin street address, latitude, longitude, free miles, maximum miles and flat shipping rate in store currency.
  • Charge once or per qualifying address in dual mode.
  • Server-side HeiGIT route API and optional US Census street-range fallback.
  • Unavailable distance rates are withheld; WooCommerce prevents orders without a valid shipping option.
  • Shortcode [milequill_shipping_rates] for checking one or two addresses, according to the configured mode.
  • Public-address diagnostic, short-lived WooCommerce session quotes and local abuse controls.
  • No trial, licensing server, telemetry or premium code.

This release supports US addresses, one shipping package per cart and Classic Checkout. Cart/Checkout Blocks, express checkout, multi-package shipments, multiple origins, international addresses and truck-specific routing are not supported. Rates and address mode are global; zone instances may customize their title and tax status. If other shipping methods are enabled in the matching zone, customers can select those methods even when distance shipping is unavailable. Virtual products that do not need shipping are unaffected. The calculator does not configure payment gateways.

External services

The plugin uses the following external services only after the administrator explicitly configures and permits them. A free Standard HeiGIT account is available; quotas and terms can change. No API subscription is sold by this plugin.

HeiGIT API / openrouteservice

Used to look up US street addresses and calculate driving-car distance. The server sends the street address and API key to https://api.heigit.org/pelias/v1/search and /search/structured. For routing, it sends origin and destination coordinates and the API key to https://api.heigit.org/openrouteservice/v2/directions/driving-car/json. No customer name, email, phone, or order ID is sent by this plugin. Addresses and coordinates may themselves be personal data. The provider receives ordinary server request metadata. HeiGIT terms restrict the transmission of personal data: do not enable customer-address processing unless the use is permitted under those terms. If this is not possible, this plugin is unsuitable for that deployment. Required provider and map-data attribution is shown below the Classic Cart/Checkout form or with standalone checker results after the administrator opts in; there is no plugin promotional credit or link.

  • Service, registration and terms: https://account.heigit.org/
  • Published API terms: https://openrouteservice.org/terms-of-service/
  • API documentation: https://api.heigit.org/
  • Privacy policy: https://heigit.org/privacy-policy/
  • Map data copyright: https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright
  • Route results license: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/

US Census Geocoder (optional)

When explicitly enabled, the plugin sends house number/street, city, state and ZIP to https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/locations/address if HeiGIT returns no matching street-level address. No Census API key is required. The service returns coordinates interpolated from street address ranges; a match is not proof of an existing building or an exact rooftop location. These coordinates are sent to HeiGIT for driving distance. Estimates within 0.5 miles of either configured fee boundary require a manual quote. The margin is a precaution, not a guarantee of accuracy.

  • Service and documentation: https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/
  • Privacy policy: https://www.census.gov/about/policies/privacy.html

Privacy

No analytics or telemetry is included. No external requests occur before provider opt-in and API configuration. API keys are stored in WordPress settings unless the server constant is used. A quote includes a keyed address/configuration hash, rate, distance estimates, status and timestamp in the WooCommerce session. Dual mode also stores the two street addresses in the checkout session for up to 10 minutes of use, so WooCommerce can recalculate rates. The checkout snapshot stores the displayed rate hash, cost and taxes. Native WooCommerce shipping-rate caches hold distance metadata, not additional raw address fields. Quotes, dual context and shortcode prefill are usable for 10 minutes; physical storage follows WooCommerce session cleanup. The prefill stores only submitted addresses, not name or email. A keyed IP hash identifies temporary rate-limit counters (10-minute expiration). Order metadata stores delivery distances, estimated status, fee, and in dual mode the submitted addresses. These records are part of order fulfillment and follow the store’s WooCommerce order retention policies. Diagnostic output is displayed only to authorized managers and is not persisted by the plugin. Deletion removes global plugin settings and registered zone instances when WooCommerce is active; order history is intentionally preserved. Remove the method from zones before deleting the plugin if WooCommerce is inactive. Custom order metadata is included in WooCommerce personal-data exports and removed when WooCommerce anonymizes an order. The administrator must provide an accurate store privacy notice and manage session and provider data rights requests. The plugin does not guarantee privacy compliance.
sections.installation:
If you tested an earlier pre-approval version under the Distance Shipping Calculator or Wajahat RouteTariff name, deactivate it first. This is a new plugin slug and settings namespace: re-enter your origin and API key, and replace old shipping-zone methods. Do not leave two versions enabled.

  1. Install and activate WooCommerce. Set up a Classic Checkout page with [woocommerce_checkout] and Classic Cart with [woocommerce_cart].
  2. Upload and activate MileQuill Distance Shipping Rates. It starts disabled. Since this pre-approval name and slug change creates a new settings namespace, re-enter your calculator settings and add the new shipping method in your zone. Do not keep old pre-release versions active.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Distance Shipping. Enter a complete US origin address and its independently verified latitude and longitude. The origin address must match the coordinates.
  4. Set free miles, maximum miles and flat rate. At or below the free limit, shipping is free. Above that limit through the maximum, the configured rate applies. Outside the maximum, the method is unavailable. Maximum must exceed the free limit.
  5. Register your own HeiGIT API key at https://account.heigit.org/ and enter it. Optionally define MILEQUILL_ORS_KEY in wp-config.php instead. Review the provider terms and privacy rules; do not enable customer-address processing unless the provider permits your use. Review and enable the optional Census fallback separately.
  6. Select Single or Dual address mode. Single uses standard WooCommerce destination fields. Dual adds optional full-address checkout fields and requires both to quote the distance method; default keys are milequill_pickup_address and milequill_delivery_address. Existing full-address billing fields can be mapped. Keep normal WooCommerce country, state, city and postcode fields configured for shipping zones and taxes. Address format: House number Street, City, ST ZIP, USA. Enter apartment/unit information separately where applicable.
  7. Enable the calculator and save. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Shipping zones. Edit a US zone, choose Add shipping method, and select MileQuill Distance Shipping Rates. Edit the method title and tax status if desired. The pricing and address mode are inherited from the calculator’s global settings.
  8. Remove any legacy zero-cost Flat rate or competing distance method from the zone if every order in that zone must meet distance rules. Other shipping options are not blocked by this plugin. Use a broad US zone for dual-address stores if required by their destination configuration. The normal WooCommerce destination selects the zone; the dual fields do not override the zone or tax address.
  9. Test free, paid, out-of-area, invalid address, changed-address, rate switching, taxes, order completion and payment on a staging store. Use the diagnostic with a public address. For dual mode, rates appear once both checkout addresses are provided. Use physical products in one shipping package.
  10. Optionally add [milequill_shipping_rates] to a page. It shows an estimate only; the actual shipping zone and tax are determined at checkout. Exclude the checker and checkout from full-page caching where necessary.
sections.faq:
Is this a shipping method?

Yes. Add MileQuill Distance Shipping Rates to a WooCommerce shipping zone. It adds an actual shipping rate, not a separate cart fee. The global settings control the rate and the zone controls availability.

Does the plugin work outside the United States?

No. This version requires US street addresses with state and ZIP. It uses driving miles only.

Why do some addresses need a manual quote?

Street-level geocoders can be incomplete. The calculator rejects missing or ambiguous street matches and never substitutes a city or ZIP centroid. Census estimates near configured boundaries also require manual review. Provider outages and quota errors block automatic orders rather than allowing an unverified price.

What happens if the API is unavailable?

The distance rate is withheld when the service cannot verify a quote. WooCommerce prevents checkout if no other shipping method is available for a shippable cart. The local test-limit reset does not reset provider quotas.

Can I use checkout blocks?

No. Use the classic WooCommerce checkout shortcode. Store API checkout using the distance method is not supported; use Classic Checkout. Other methods are not intentionally blocked.
sections.changelog:
1.2.1

  • Use the distinctive MileQuill Distance Shipping Rates brand and new milequill-prefixed identifiers, shortcode, text domain and shipping method.
  • No changes to distance pricing rules or API integration. Reconfigure pre-release installations after changing slugs.

1.2.0

  • Adopt a distinctive plugin name and slug, with unique prefixed declarations, data keys, and handles as requested by directory reviewers.
  • Use a new settings namespace and shipping method identifier. After upgrading a pre-approval development installation, re-enter settings and add the new shipping method to each zone.

1.1.4

  • Add plugin author and WordPress.org contributor information.

1.1.3

  • Sanitize and validate diagnostic and standalone checker POST address inputs before use.
  • Escape the translated Classic Checkout exception message.
  • Add WordPress compatibility metadata to the readme.

1.1.2

  • Explicit zero-cost shipping price and Free Delivery label for distance rates.
  • Moved provider attribution out of the shipping-rate row to below the Classic Cart/Checkout form; standalone checker attribution remains visible.

1.1.1

  • Diagnostic now reports saved distance limits, rate and eligibility for the tested address.
  • Out-of-area checkout notice shows the calculated distance and maximum allowed distance.
  • Version change invalidates previous quote fingerprints.

1.1.0

  • Registered native WooCommerce shipping-zone method; removed separate fee.
  • Added zone title/tax settings, shipping package fingerprint, rate metadata, and checkout rate validation.
  • Preserved single/dual address settings and shortcode.

1.0.0

  • Initial generic release: configurable origin, distance thresholds, fee, address modes, diagnostics, external service opt-ins, and checkout validation.
